report.finding: Unauthorized root SSH login and backdoor account creation on kubsdb at 03:12–03:13 UTC. An external IP (203.0.113.45) authenticated as root via password, created a new user "svc-backup" with a home directory and bash shell, and disconnected 49 seconds later. The attack was enabled by a leftover temporary sshd drop-in config (/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-temp.conf) that overrides the secure defaults (PermitRootLogin prohibit-password, PasswordAuthentication no) to allow root password login. The svc-backup account has no corresponding korg work item, no cron entries, and no other references — it appears to be a persistence backdoor.

No korg items reference svc-backup, 203.0.113.45, or any backup-related work. No other auth events in the overnight window.
report.next_step: Ken should immediately: (1) Remove /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-temp.conf and reload sshd to restore secure defaults. (2) Lock or delete the svc-backup account (userdel -r svc-backup). (3) Rotate the root password and any other credentials on kubsdb. (4) Check for additional persistence (authorized_keys, cron, systemd units, .bashrc modifications). (5) Block 203.0.113.45 at the firewall. (6) File a korg incident item documenting the timeline. (7) Review whether the temp sshd override was placed intentionally (e.g., for a one-off maintenance task) and why it was never removed.
